title: Implementing the Decision-Aid for Lupus (IDEAL Strategy)
off: Implementing the Decision-Aid for Lupus (IDEAL Strategy)
summary: The study will attempt to put into practice a shared decision making (SDM) strategy, using an individualized, computerized decision- aid (DA) for Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
desc: The proposed study will evaluate methods to implement a shared decision making strategy, using an individualized, computerized decision- aid (DA). The investigators will test the effectiveness of this implementation with 3 strategies in 15 clinics. Formative evaluation strategies will be used to assess needs at each clinic, with key clinic informants participating in semi-structured interviews. The study will enroll patient participants across all 16 sites, who will review the decision aid and be asked a feasibility and acceptability assessment. At the conclusion of the study, key clinic informants, as well as selected patient participants will participate in semi-structured interviews to assess the effectiveness in implementing the DA in the clinic setting.
elig:
Patient Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults with a diagnosis of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) by a rheumatologist

Patient Exclusion Criteria:

* No diagnosis of lupus, not English or Spanish speaking, visually impaired, altered mental status

arms.d: All adult lupus patients, regardless of if they are having an active flare

primary.m: Penetration/Reach: Number of Eligible Participants at Each Clinical Site Who Enrolled Divided by the Number of Eligible Participants at Each Clinical Site, Expressed as Overall Percent
